title: 持续交付 第 1 章 · 软件交付的难题 — 专业书籍精读 Book 13
title_en: Continuous Delivery Ch 1 · The Problem of Delivering Software — Books Deep-Read 13

questions.question: 关于「发布为什么危险」，《持续交付》第 1 章提出的反直觉因果是？
options: 发布危险是因为生产环境本身就比测试环境复杂得多，无法避免
发布危险是因为开发人员写的代码质量不够高，测试也不足
不是改动大所以危险，而是发布得少，每次改动才那么大
发布本质上就有风险，越少发布，累积的风险也就越小
questions.explanation: 根源在于发布过程手工、罕见、不可重复。「越少发布风险越小」正是被本章反驳的常识，所以有了「痛就更频繁地做它」。
questions.question_en: On why releases are dangerous, what counterintuitive causality does chapter 1 of Continuous Delivery put forward?
options_en: Releases are risky because production is inherently far more complex than test, which can't be avoided
Releases are risky because developers' code quality is too low and testing is inadequate
It's not that big changes make releases risky; releasing rarely is what makes each change so big
Releasing is inherently risky, so the fewer releases you do, the less risk accumulates
questions.explanation_en: The root cause is a release process that is manual, rare and unrepeatable. "Fewer releases, less risk" is exactly the common sense this chapter refutes, hence "if it hurts, do it more often."

questions.question: 一家公司搭好了流水线，每个通过全部关卡的构建都可以上线，但什么时候真正发给用户由业务方决定。按本章的区分，这是？
options: 持续集成：每天把改动合回主干并自动构建测试，就是这个意思
持续部署：只要流水线全部通过，就已经等于自动部署到了生产环境上
持续交付：每个通过的构建都具备上线资格，按不按按钮是业务决策
还不算持续交付：必须让每个通过的构建自动进入生产才算数
questions.explanation: 本书主张的正是中间那一档：具备上线资格，由业务按按钮。自动直推生产是更激进的持续部署，并非所有产品都适用。
questions.question_en: A company has a pipeline where every build that passes all stages can go live, but the business decides when users actually get it. By the chapter's distinctions, what is this?
options_en: Continuous integration: merging to trunk daily with automated build and test is exactly this
Continuous deployment: passing the whole pipeline already amounts to being deployed to production
Continuous delivery: every passing build is releasable, and pressing the button is a business decision
Not yet continuous delivery: every passing build must go to production automatically to count
questions.explanation_en: This is the middle tier the book advocates: releasable, with the business pressing the button. Pushing automatically to production is the more aggressive continuous deployment, which doesn't suit every product.

questions.question: 本章说「每一次签入都产生一个潜在的发布版本」。这带来的关键转变是？
options: 「能不能发」从人拍板的里程碑，变成流水线随时回答的状态，每关都在证伪它
每次签入都必须立刻发布到生产环境，不再需要任何人工判断
开发人员签入前必须自己完成全部测试，确保代码可以直接发布
测试全部完成之后，再由团队从多个构建中提名一个发布候选版，并跑一遍完整回归
questions.explanation: 传统做法是末端由人提名候选版；本章反过来，让每个构建默认都是候选，流水线逐关淘汰。这不等于每次签入都自动上线，那是持续部署。
questions.question_en: The chapter says "every check-in produces a potential release." What key shift does this bring?
options_en: "Can we ship?" stops being a milestone a person decides and becomes a status the pipeline answers anytime, each stage trying to falsify it
Every check-in must be released to production immediately, with no further human judgment
Developers must finish all testing themselves before checking in, so the code can ship directly
After testing, the team nominates one release candidate from several builds and runs a full regression
questions.explanation_en: Traditionally a person nominates a candidate at the end; here every build is a candidate by default and the pipeline weeds them out stage by stage. That doesn't mean every check-in auto-deploys; that would be continuous deployment.
